Latent View Analytics | Q1 FY27 Concall Highlights

Financial Performance
- FY27 revenue growth guidance 12% maintained.
- Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance 20–21%.
- Strong QoQ recovery expected in Q2 FY27.
- Continued investments in AI capabilities.

Operational Highlights
- Consumer Goods business expected to grow 25%+ QoQ.
- Consumer Goods pipeline at ~US$26 million.
- Project extensions worth ~US$2 million.
- Technology pipeline exceeds US$15 million.
- Over 35% of Q1 work AI-led.
- 80% of client engagements included AI.
- Clients shifting from AI pilots to production.

Management Guidance
- FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained.
- Long-term target US$200 million annual revenue.
- Target timeline FY28/FY29.
- Growth through organic expansion.
- Targeted acquisitions in Healthcare.
- Expansion into Life Sciences.
- Focus on Data Engineering.

Key Positives
- Strong confidence in Q2 recovery.
- Pursuing 14+ large deals.
- Each deal potential ~US$500K.
- AI demand accelerating.
- Acquisition discussions progressing.

Key Concerns
- Q1 execution remained soft.
- Pipeline conversion critical.
- Margin discipline to be maintained.
- AI investments may pressure margins.

Key Monitorables
- Q2 revenue recovery.
- Consumer Goods pipeline conversion.
- Technology deal conversion.
- Healthcare acquisitions.
- AI-led enterprise deployments.

Impact
- Positive.
- AI demand remains robust.
- Healthy deal pipeline.
- Strong medium-term visibility.
- Execution remains key.

Key Takeaway
- Latent View maintained its FY27 guidance and expects a strong Q2 recovery, supported by a healthy AI-led deal pipeline, increasing enterprise AI adoption, and strategic acquisitions, while execution and pipeline conversion remain the key factors to watch.

MOTILAL OSWAL: MARKET MAY BE NEARING A BOTTOM, UPSIDE TRIGGERS BUILDING 📈

• 📊 Valuations have turned attractive with Nifty PE at 18.8x (below 20-year average of 19.6x), while Market Cap-to-GDP has corrected to 120% from 170%

• 💰 Corporate Profit-to-GDP has improved to 7.8–7.9%, the highest since 2008, but with much stronger corporate balance sheets this time

• 📈 Q1 earnings remain strong, with 211 companies under MoFSL coverage reporting 17% earnings growth versus 13% estimates, raising prospects of earnings upgrades

• 🌍 Global headwinds are easing as FPI outflows normalize, Middle East tensions stabilize, crude remains around $84, and $37 billion FCNR deposits support the rupee

• 🚗 Domestic indicators remain supportive with improving auto sales, rising reservoir levels, and Nifty reclaiming its 200-DEMA for the first time since February 2026

• ⚠️ Large IPOs, QIPs and block deals may absorb liquidity, limiting sharp market rallies in the near term

🟢 View: Positive (MoFSL believes downside is limited, with the next 3–4 months critical for confirmation through sustained earnings, stable crude, FCNR inflows and monsoon progress.)

ANGEL ONE , GROWW ,ANAND RATHI SHARES; F&O CLOSING AUCTION NORMS MAY HIT BROKING REVENUE 📉

• ⚠️ New F&O closing auction shifts continuous trading end to 3:15 PM, impacting broker income

• 📉 Angel One may see 1–3% impact on broking revenue, while Zerodha estimates a 1–5% hit

• 🤖 High-frequency traders (HFTs) and jobbers likely to lose easy closing-session liquidity

• 🛡️ New mechanism reduces last-minute price manipulation, lowers volatility and strengthens closing price discovery

• 🏛️ Impact on BSE, CDSL, NSDL and KFin Technologies is expected to remain largely neutral

🟠 Impact: Negative (For broking firms and HFT participants due to lower trading opportunities and brokerage income.)

Aimtron : Initiation of coverage by Nuvama (31 July 2026)

AIMTRON focuses on high-value, niche markets, and specialty businesses rather than competing in high-volume, low-margin segments. Its focus has been on critical nature industries in the industrial EMS segment as it evolves from a pure play PCB assembler to a box-build and original design manufacturer.

AIMTRON operates in the industrial B2B EMS space, where lower volumes are offset by better pricing given the complex, safety-critical, and customised nature of products, as reflected in its industry-leading margin and returns. Despite delivering the fastest growth vis-à-vis its peers, it trades cheaper at 17.3x FY28E EV/EBITDA and 27.2x P/E. The stock currently trades at a significant discount to its B2B ESDM peer set which we believe will close as the company scales. We initiate with a ‘BUY’ rating valuing the company at 40x FY28E diluted EPS of INR 50.9 resulting in a target price of INR 2,036.

AIC acquisition to bolster US presence : 

The acquisition provides AIMTRON with four SMT lines, with end-to-end capabilities, in a 58,000 sq. ft. manufacturing facility. It also has 3.9 acres of land available for future expansion. AIC’s expertise lies in high-reliability electronics, ruggedised products, and box-build manufacturing. The facility is close to major industrial OEMs such as Caterpillar, Deere & Company, CNH Industrial, and Bunn-O-Matic Corporation, thus providing a much faster route to expanding its US manufacturing footprint than building a greenfield facility.

AIC generated USD16.9mn (~INR160cr) of revenue in CY2025 and contributed USD1.6mn (~INR15cr) to the group's consolidated revenue during its first two months of consolidation in FY26 (February–March). During this period, its revenue was primarily driven by ruggedised electronics (26%), meditech (19%), BESS (17.8%), and defence (17.1%), highlighting strong strategic alignment with AIMTRON's core business. From a product mix perspective, PCBA/box-build solutions accounted for 64.9%/35.1% of revenue.

The management expects utilisation to scale to 90% from 54%, increasing its annual revenue potential to USD25–30mn (INR280–300cr) over the next three years. While AIC operated at an EBITDA margin of ~11% at the time of its acquisition, it expects to quickly ramp up to standalone margin levels within two years and expects the business to be EPS accretive from the first year.

Greenfield expansion to enhance ESDM positioning

The new facility will add six SMT lines in a phased manner and will also house a dedicated ODM, R&D, and defence zone to strengthen its engineering and high-precision manufacturing capabilities.

The project is being funded through preferential warrants (INR94.6cr) and internal accruals. The facility is expected to turn operational in phases from Q3 or Q4FY27, with the commissioning of the SMT line targeted by Q4FY27 or Q1FY28. On completion, the expansion is expected to potentially add ~INR500cr of annual revenue to the existing INR800–900cr over time.

NSE | Revised Trading Timings (Effective 3 Aug 2026)

Key Changes
- Normal cash market closes at 3:30 PM.
- FnO stocks (cash segment) stop at 3:15 PM.
- Futures & Options trade until 3:40 PM.
- Closing Auction runs 3:15–3:30 PM.
- Auction determines official closing price.

What Traders Should Know
- Don't assume FnO ends at 3:30 PM.
- Check broker auto square-off timings.
- Expect higher activity after 3:30 PM.
- Option traders should monitor final minutes.
- Closing price impacts derivatives settlement.

Impact
- Important.
- Better price discovery.
- Revised execution timings.
- Increased closing volatility.
- Requires trading plan adjustments.

Key Takeaway
- From 3 August 2026, FnO cash-market stocks stop trading at 3:15 PM, a Closing Auction runs until 3:30 PM, and Futures & Options continue trading until 3:40 PM, making it essential for derivatives traders to adapt their execution strategy.

Sterlite Tech: Nuvama Report and my thoughts

Nuvama has come up with an updated report on Sterlite Tech with a price target of 770.

Their earlier price target was 440, which they increased to 770 after Q11FY27 results..
That's an upgrade of 75%
Just imagine the amount of earnings surprise.

Before Q1Fy27 results, many brokerages were expecting Sterlite to generate a PAT of 400-500 crores in FY27
Now, the same brokerages are estimating FY27 PAT to be 900-100 Crores, almost an increase of 100%

Nuvama report estimates Fy27 PAT of 906 Cr.
However, this is still conservative and below the management guidance  - Nuvama has considered EBITDA margins of 20.3% whereas Company has guided for 23%

Also, Sterlite recently did a QIP of 1500 Cr. While this will lead to a dilution of 5%, the entire debt is gone on one shot and it has become a net cash company !!

Personally, I think Sterlite would cross 1000 Cr PAT for FY 27 easily and might hit 1100 Cr.

Now, the interesting part - valuations
Before Q1FY27 results, Sterlite was trading at a trailing PE of 500+. Many people looked at screener PE, and shouted bubble !!
Now, PE has already dropped to 121
On FY27 basis - Sterlite is trading at a PE of 30-32
Half of the stocks in the Indian market are trading at higher valuations !!

Always consider forward earnings and valuations.
Particularly for turnaround cases like Sterlite, it is futile to look at trailing PE !!

So why did PBT jump +138% and PAT +156% when EBITDA fell?

The gap sits almost entirely below EBITDA and is non-operating. 

The clue is the "share of profit of Joint Ventures" line and the reconciliation: PBT of ₹868.98 Cr is far above what ₹463 Cr of EBITDA minus ₹107 Cr depreciation minus ₹24 Cr finance cost (≈₹332 Cr operating PBT) would produce. 

The ~₹537 Cr difference comes from other income of ₹528.29 Cr — which exploded from just ₹1.68 Cr a year ago. 

That single line is the entire story of the profit surge. 

A ₹528 Cr other-income figure on this base is not routine treasury income; 

it's almost certainly a one-off/exceptional item (a fair-value gain, a stake revaluation, a divestment/JV-related gain, or similar). Because your EBITDA definition strips other income, EBITDA correctly shows the flat operating reality while PBT/PAT capture the windfall.

This is the trickiest quarter of the set, and the headline EPS (+154%) and PBT (+138%) badly overstate the operating quarter — read it carefully. Revenue grew a strong +21% YoY, consistent with continued EMS/mobile ramp, and operationally that's the real story. But operating EBITDA actually fell ~4% YoY, and the EBITDA margin compressed to 2.98% from 3.76% — a ~78 bps decline. 

For a thin-margin assembler this is the line that matters: the revenue mix is shifting even more toward ultra-low-margin, high-value mobile assembly (BOM pass-through), which dilutes the blended margin even as it inflates the topline. So the operating engine ran roughly flat-to-slightly-down YoY on absolute EBITDA despite 21% more revenue — the opposite of what the EPS suggests.

EU demand would be monitored given adverse weather trends (though 1Q volumes were healthy).

In US, there is strong headroom for growth, given duty has stabilized at 10%.

That said, geopolitical environment remains volatile, manifesting in logistics-related challenges and rising raw material costs.

• Europe profitability remains the key monitorable going forward

• India business profitability remained strong

• Management's commentary on the Europe profitability outlook will be crucial

• The stock is expected to perform broadly in line with the market

MACQUARIE ON MANKIND PHARMA

Recommendation: Underperform
Target Price: ₹2,080

Key Takeaways:

• Q1 FY27 results were largely in line with expectations

• Domestic business underperformance continues to remain a key concern

MORGAN STANLEY ON NIVA BUPA

Recommendation: Equal-weight
Target Price: ₹91

Key Takeaways:

• Q1 delivered another strong quarter

• Loss ratio improved due to the non-renewal of large group business contracts with unfavorable economics

• The company continues to deliver strong profitability and top-line growth, but upside appears limited

MORGAN STANLEY ON TATA STEEL

Recommendation: Overweight
Target Price: ₹235

Key Takeaways:

• Strong domestic steel realizations were largely offset by higher operating costs

• Consolidated EBITDA came in 11% below consensus estimates

• Raw material costs increased, led by higher coking coal consumption costs

MACQUARIE ON WESTLIFE FOODWORLD

Recommendation: Outperform
Target Price: ₹520

Key Takeaways:

• Q1 results were largely in line; growth outlook remains constructive

• Positive on multiple long-term growth tailwinds supporting the business

• Key risks include input cost inflation and any slowdown in consumer demand

CITI ON MGL

Recommendation: Accumulate
Target Price: ₹1,400

Key Takeaways:

• Performance remained impressive despite gas supply challenges arising from the West Asia conflict

• Volume growth exceeded expectations, driven by strong CNG demand

• Robust CNG volume growth offset the impact of price hikes across segments

JEFFERIES ON SYRMA SGS

Recommendation: Hold
Target Price: ₹1,430 (Earlier ₹1,185)

Key Takeaways:

• Strong quarter, but much of the upside is already reflected in the stock price

• Recommends caution after the sharp rally

• Raised FY27–FY29 EPS estimates by 12–13%; expects 33% EPS CAGR

• Healthy operating leverage supported EBITDA margin expansion

• Performance remains in line with Syrma's FY27 growth outlook of 30–35%

MACQUARIE ON SWIGGY

Recommendation: Underperform
Target Price: ₹230

Key Takeaways:

• Expects slower growth and higher cash burn

• Swiggy has outlined a path to adjusted EBITDA breakeven for Instamart, but the timeline and trajectory remain unclear

• Recent leadership changes at Instamart make the breakeven target appear aspirational rather than the base case

CITI ON EXIDE

Recommendation: Accumulate
Target Price: ₹410

Key Takeaways:

• Q1 results came in significantly above estimates

• Healthy revenue growth across all key segments

• Price hikes and a better product mix offset the impact of higher commodity costs on gross margins

• Strong operating leverage further supported EBITDA margin expansion

MORGAN STANLEY ON MGL

Recommendation: Overweight
Target Price: ₹1,421

Key Takeaways:

• Growth exceeded expectations, driven by strong volume growth

• Earnings beat supported by CNG retail price hikes and US gas sourcing exposure

• Unit margins improved due to lower Henry Hub gas prices and a ₹5/kg CNG price hike

• OMC under-recoveries are likely to keep fuel prices elevated, supporting CNG demand

CITI ON SWIGGY

Recommendation: Accumulate
Target Price: ₹390 (Earlier: ₹415)

Key Takeaways:

• Quick commerce continues to accelerate, with contribution margin breakeven expected ahead despite a Q1 miss

• Swiggy is shifting its strategy to maximize growth while maintaining contribution margin breakeven, instead of prioritizing breakeven above all else

• Food delivery growth was slightly soft, but margins remained healthy

HSBC ON SEDEMAC MECHATRONICS

Recommendation: Accumulate
Target Price: ₹3,700

Key Takeaways:

• R&D-driven innovation supports long-term revenue compounding

• Advanced sensor-less motor control technology for 2W/3W starter systems has been a key growth driver

• Diversification into EVs, power tools and commercial vehicles is expected to sustain growth momentum

• Strong R&D capabilities and growth trajectory justify a premium valuation

JEFFERIES ON HEXAWARE

Recommendation: Underperform
Target Price: ₹500 (Earlier: ₹480)

Key Takeaways:

• Weak growth outlook persists

• Cut revenue and EPS estimates by up to 7% after Q2 miss and weaker-than-expected CY26 growth guidance of 6–7%

• Worsening growth outlook and execution raise concerns over sustaining the current valuation multiple of 22x PE
